found_by: the read-write fuzzer (nightly, an hour of fuzz-rw): AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 1 in ext4_bmap_bit_find_clr (ext4_bitmap.c:136), reached from ext4_ialloc_alloc_inode -> ext4_fs_alloc_inode -> ext4b_create
base: mke2fs -t ext4 -b 1024 -g 1024 (5 block groups, 256 inodes/group, ^metadata_csum so no checksum to re-stamp)
symptom: The blocks geometry implies 5 groups; the inode count now covers only 1. ext4_inodes_in_group_cnt sizes the last group as inode_count - (groups-1) x inodes_per_group = 256 - 4 x 256, which underflows to about four billion. Once the early groups fill, the next create scans a one-block inode bitmap for that many bits and reads straight off the end of the block. The minimised fuzzer reproducer needs an evolved allocator state to reach the last group; this crafted image trips the same geometry deterministically at probe.
fixed_by: the geometry gate requires inode_count == block groups x inodes_per_group, exactly -- the Linux kernel's own rule (Core/shim/ext4_bridge.c). The first version refused only the too-small side; fixture 0022 is the other.
reproduce: build/bin/ext4dump probe # must be UNSUPPORTED, naming the inode count
